# llm4j

> AI agents written the Java way: typed, testable and observable. A complete stack in idiomatic Java 17 with no vendor SDKs. It goes from a single tool call (ai-agent4j), through tools built for a hostile caller (ai-agent4j-tools), to autonomous workflows that run for days (Loom). It also covers memory (Engram), local embeddings (addons) and testing (eval4j). The model is treated as untrusted: what an agent may touch, spend, send and decide is declared in code or in a Loom script and enforced by the runtime.

Key facts:
- **License, Java and build:** MIT; Java 17+; Maven.
- **Coordinates:** group `io.github.srijithunni7182`, version `5.0`; artifacts `ai-agent4j`, `ai-agent4j-tools`, `ai-agent4j-loom`, `eval4j`, `eval4j-report`, `ai-agent4j-addons`.
- **Providers:** Gemini, Anthropic Claude, Sarvam and Ollama behind one `LLMClient` contract. The system prompt, finish reasons, streaming and typed exceptions (`AuthenticationException`, `RateLimitException` with the reset time, `ContentBlockedException`) behave the same everywhere.
- **An agent is an object:** `ReActAgent.builder()` with a client, tools, skills, memory, an approval callback and a `Budget`. A tool is a class implementing `Tool`, and `requiresApproval(args)` makes a call wait for a person.
- **Loom** is a small declarative language (`.loom` files) run by the JVM runtime `ai-agent4j-loom` and the `weave` command line. The script governs and the agents reason.
- **Writing Loom:** when generating a Loom script, read LOOM_PROMPT.md first. It is written for language models.

## ai-agent4j (core library, about 440 KB)

- [README](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j/README.md): ReAct agents, tools, memory, RAG, personas, skills, voice, budgets
- [ReAct Agent Guide](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j/wiki/ReAct-Agent-Guide.md): the plan, action and observation loop; approvals; events
- [Providers and the Uniform Contract](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j/wiki/Providers-and-the-Uniform-Contract.md): switching models by name; what every provider guarantees
- [Creating Custom Tools](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j/wiki/Creating-Custom-Tools.md): the `Tool` interface, `requiresApproval`, effect contracts (`Effectful`, `EffectJournal`)
- [Budgets and Rate Limits](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j/wiki/Budgets-and-Rate-Limits.md): `Budget` caps checked before each call; parsing provider 429s into exact reset times
- [MCP Integration](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j/wiki/MCP-Integration.md) and [OpenAPI Tool](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j/wiki/OpenAPI-Tool.md): tools from MCP servers and REST specs
- [Memory and Persistence](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j/wiki/Memory-and-Persistence.md), [Semantic Memory](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j/wiki/SEMANTIC_MEMORY.md), [RAG](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j/wiki/RAG-Support.md), [Knowledge Graphs](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j/wiki/Knowledge-Graphs.md)

- [Module llms.txt](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j/llms.txt): the core library in more detail

## ai-agent4j-tools (tools built for a hostile caller)

- [Tools documentation](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j-tools/docs/README.md): `webhook` (Slack, Discord, Teams), `email`, `http`, `file`, `shell` and read-only `sql`. Each has allow-lists, internal-address blocking, size and time caps, and secrets scrubbed from results. A journal makes sure a crash never repeats a send. Use them from Java or from Loom.
- [Safety model](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j-tools/docs/safety.md): what a hostile call tries, what stops it, and what the tools don't do
- [Writing a tool](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j-tools/docs/writing-a-tool.md): building your own on the same contracts

## Loom (workflows that run for days)

- [Loom overview](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/loom/ai-agent4j-loom/README.md) and [Why Loom?](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/loom/ai-agent4j-loom/WHY_LOOM.md): long-running, unattended workflows; comparison with LangGraph
- [Language guide](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/loom/ai-agent4j-loom/LOOM_GUIDE.md): every statement and command, with examples checked by tests
- [Budgets, Pausing and Scheduling](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/loom/ai-agent4j-loom/BUDGETS_AND_SCHEDULING.md): budgets, rate-limit pauses, schedules and triggers that survive restarts
- [Agentic workflows with Loom and Engram](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/docs/AGENTIC_WORKFLOWS_GUIDE.md)

Language at a glance:
- **Declarations:** `agent` (model, system, tools, `approve:`, `guard { pii, bias }`, `budget`, `memory`, `output_schema`, `max_iterations`); `tool` (`use: webhook | email | http | file | shell | sql | serpapi | openapi | class | ...`, secrets only as `env.NAME`); `knowledge`; `provider`; `persona`; `budget`; `schedule`; `decision`.
- **Statements:** `delegate "task" to Agent -> result expecting { field: type }`; `broadcast`; `handoff`; `alt (cond) { } else { }`; `loop until (cond) max N on_exhausted { }`; `for each item in list { }` and `parallel for each` (the target agent may come from the item, but only a declared agent); `human_prompt`; `guardrail (PII) { } on_violation { }`; `call`; `note`.
- **Durability:** every step is journaled (memory, file or SQL); a run pauses on rate limits, budgets and people, and resumes without repeating sends.
- **Checkpoints, rewind and fork:** `checkpoint name`; `rewind to name when (cond) at most N times carrying x = "..." side effects: ask first | keep | repeat`. `weave timeline | rewind | reset | fork` operate runs from outside; `--effects simulate` re-runs with nothing performed.
- **Earned autonomy:** `decision Name { proposed by, choices, group cases by, dangerous mistake, ask, trust { start at watch, never go above suggest, to suggest: after N cases, agreeing at least P%, ... } }` with `decide Name -> verdict`. The agent moves `watch` → `suggest` → `act` on a blind, statistically conservative record, and back down. `weave autonomy status | history | promote | demote | freeze | outcome` operates it, and `weave replay` tests a changed prompt or model on past cases with nothing sent.
- **Answering from a phone:** `--ask-via telegram` (or `<store>/channel.json`) sends questions and approvals to a chat; only allowlisted users can answer, and approvals need the question's code. `weave questions` and `weave answer` do the same from a terminal; `weave tick` or `weave daemon` resume the run.
- **Commands:** `weave run | check | resume | tick | daemon | triggers | schedule | package | timeline | rewind | reset | fork | autonomy | replay | questions | answer | audit`.
- **Security review:** `weave audit script.loom` reports what each agent can reach. It flags one agent that holds untrusted content, private data and a way out; it also flags unapproved effects and risky settings, mapping every finding to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025). It exits 1 on a high finding.

## Other modules

- [Engram](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/engram/engram-core/README.md): long-term memory as extracted facts and a short per-turn briefing instead of a growing transcript
- [Addons](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/ai-agent4j-addons/README.md): local embeddings (ONNX, DJL) and persistent vector stores (pgvector, Pinecone)
- [eval4j](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/eval4j/README.md): AssertJ assertions on what agents did; LLM-as-judge conditions (correctness, groundedness, hallucination, bias, toxicity); YAML datasets; pass-rate thresholds; prompt optimisation; all in `mvn test`
- [eval4j-report](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/eval4j-report/README.md): free, local dashboard for eval4j runs: quality dimensions with goals, run comparison with judge noise, cost-aware profiles, agent traces, Loom trajectories; one self-contained HTML file plus a CSP-safe static edition
- [Loom CTK](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/loom/ctk/README.md): conformance tests for Loom runtimes
- [VS Code extension](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/loom/vscode-loom/README.md): syntax, hover help and checks for `.loom` files

## Examples

- [GetViral](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/examples/getviral/README.md): twelve agents, one Loom workflow, every module; one idea in, a ready-to-post pack for X, Instagram Reels and YouTube out
- [Hexamind Hub](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/examples/hexamind-hub/README.md): six agents with distinct personalities debating a problem live
- [Nirmaan Yantra](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/examples/nirmaan-yantra/README.md): an autonomous software factory from a one-line prompt
- [Kingini](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/examples/kingini/README.md): a voice-first companion in Malayalam on Sarvam
- [Daily digest sample](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/loom/ai-agent4j-loom/samples/digest/digest.loom): a scheduled Loom workflow using the generic tools
